layers.title: What the model postulates
layers.lead: The setting is assumed, not derived: a two-time bulk, two shadows — a visible one and a mirror one, each with its own time — and the bridges between them. Each shadow’s seven internal dimensions form the geometry derived below.
items: The bulk is 26-dimensional with signature (24,2), one time per 13D shadow of signature (12,1).
Twelve bridges: the directed edges of K<sub>4</sub> on a Fano arc of four faces, grouped into three E<sub>8</sub> blocks.
WA-1 (adopted 2026-10-01): one bridge per resolved A<sub>1</sub> component (one U(1)). With the 3 × 4 bridge-component match it selects (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (12, 43) without data (CG.12).

layers.title: Standard physics it builds on
layers.lead: Established results the model uses, each with its source:
items: M-theory on a compact 7-manifold with holonomy G<sub>2</sub> gives 4D N = 1 supergravity with b<sub>2</sub> abelian vector multiplets and b<sub>3</sub> neutral chiral multiplets (Acharya 1999; Lukas & Morris 2004).

Compact 7-manifolds with a torsion-free G<sub>2</sub>-structure are obtained by resolving T<sup>7</sup>/Γ with Eguchi-Hanson spaces; the (ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup> example has b<sub>2</sub> = 12, b<sub>3</sub> = 43, and further examples include b<sub>2</sub> = 8 + l, b<sub>3</sub> = 47 - l (Joyce 1996a; Joyce 1996b; Joyce 2000).
For a compact torsion-free G<sub>2</sub>-structure, Hol = G<sub>2</sub> iff π<sub>1</sub> is finite (Joyce, JDG II, Prop. 1.1.1) (Joyce 1996b).
π<sub>1</sub> of a quotient space is the group modulo the subgroup generated by elements with fixed points (Armstrong 1968).
An A<sub>1</sub> singularity fibred over a 3-manifold Q carries pure N = (1 + b<sub>1</sub>(Q)) super Yang-Mills (Acharya 1999).
G<sub>4</sub> flux on a smooth G<sub>2</sub> manifold gives a positive runaway potential; a supersymmetric vacuum needs a non-real Chern-Simons invariant (Acharya et al. 2005; Lukas & Morris 2004).
M-theory on Joyce manifolds, as K3 fibrations, is dual to heterotic strings on T<sup>3</sup>-fibred Calabi-Yau threefolds (Acharya 1996).

layers.title: How the geometry is selected
layers.lead: Each step follows from the one before; theorem CG.12 states the chain as one result, and each switch it rests on can be flipped to compare the alternative.
items: φ, the model’s 3-form, fixes the folding group Γ = (ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup>: the coordinate sign-flips that preserve all seven of its terms.

Joyce’s construction from Γ reaches 28 literature-checked Betti pairs (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>), on the lines b<sub>2</sub> + b<sub>3</sub> = 23, 39 and 55 and the point (0, 7); the earlier seed b<sub>3</sub> = 24 is not among them (CG.7).

Across that family the restricted holonomy climbs trivial → SU(2) → SU(3) → G<sub>2</sub> as the number n of singular involutions goes 0 → 3, and π<sub>1</sub> is finite only at n = 3. On the compact real form of φ — the active path (D-015) — that makes the holonomy exactly G<sub>2</sub> only on the n = 3 line.

On that line the twelve bridges of the bulk and the twelve singular components of Y<sub>7</sub> form one 3 × 4 structure only on the all-plain classes, at (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (12, 43). Identifying each bridge with one component (WA-1, adopted 2026-10-01) selects it without using data (CG.12).
n<sub>gen</sub> = b<sub>2</sub>/4 = 3, the number of singular involutions: three generations is the rank of the folding group, not a fitted number.

layers.title: The closed geometry, proved
layers.lead: Y<sub>7</sub> is Joyce’s resolution of T<sup>7</sup>/(ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup>, with (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (12, 43) and Betti numbers (1, 0, 12, 43, 43, 12, 0, 1). Each statement below is a theorem with a proof, a test and a falsifier (13 of 13 hold); together they fix the topology and every discrete datum with no free parameter. The metric’s b<sub>3</sub> moduli are fields, not parameters, and their stabilisation is open.
items: CG.1 Resolved Betti numbers of Y7
CG.2 Euler characteristic of Y7
CG.3 Singular components of T7/Γ
CG.4 Fundamental group of Y7 across the family
CG.5 Gauge content of Y7
CG.6 G4 flux fixes no modulus of Y7 at leading order
CG.7 What Joyce's construction reaches from φ's (ℤ/2)3
CG.8 The 12 bridges and the 12 A1 components are one structure
CG.9 One Kummer K3 per singular involution

layers.title: What the model found
layers.lead: Results of the model’s own computations, each with its test:
items: Joyce's construction from φ's diagonal (ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup> reaches 28 literature-checked (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>); the off-path seed b<sub>3</sub> = 24 is not among them (Joyce 1996b).
Across the family, restricted holonomy is trivial, SU(2), SU(3), G<sub>2</sub> for n = 0..3 singular involutions; π<sub>1</sub> is finite only at n = 3 (Joyce 1996b).

The 12 bridges and the 12 A<sub>1</sub> components form one 3 × 4 structure, existing exactly on the all-plain members; blocks match involutions canonically, while the matching inside a block is a free choice.
χ<sub>eff</sub> = 2 × sum over singular involutions of χ(Kummer K3) = 48n; n<sub>gen</sub> = χ<sub>eff</sub>/48 counts singular involutions (adopted 2026-10-01).
In φ's Joyce family, holonomy exactly G<sub>2</sub> and a confining gauge sector are mutually exclusive (Acharya 1999).

layers.title: What was corrected
layers.lead: Earlier claims of the model that were wrong, and what replaced them:
items: The adopted 3-form was the split real form, one transcription sign away from the framework's own octonion product. The compact form is the active path since 2026-10-01; the split form stays switchable.
The A<sub>1</sub> filter tested the setwise stabiliser; the four-member family was the all-plain subfamily of Joyce's construction (Joyce 1996b).
Constants built on k_gimel = b<sub>3</sub>/2 + 1/π were fits made at the retired seed, not derivations.

χ<sub>eff</sub> = 144 was called the Euler characteristic of the G<sub>2</sub> manifold. Every closed odd-dimensional manifold has χ = 0, so χ<sub>eff</sub> is an effective index, now defined by the K3 reading, 48 n (adopted 2026-10-01).

The internal space was formerly described as a twisted connected sum ('TCS #187') with b<sub>3</sub> = 24. No published TCS enumeration has such an entry, and b<sub>3</sub> = 24 lies below the published TCS ranges. The construction is Joyce's orbifold resolution, which reaches b<sub>3</sub> = 43 and never 24 (Joyce 1996b).

The racetrack exponent a = 2 π / b<sub>3</sub> read a Betti number as the rank of a gauge group. Y<sub>7</sub>'s singular loci carry N = 4 super Yang-Mills, and with full holonomy no confining sector exists in φ's Joyce family, so Y<sub>7</sub> has no gaugino racetrack; its values were calibrations at the off-path seed (Acharya 1999).

Two borrowed claims were withdrawn (signature ruling 2026-08-31): Bars' Sp(2,ℝ) ghost-freedom theorem, because gauging (24,2) gives one (23,1) shadow rather than two (12,1) shadows; and '26 = the bosonic critical dimension', because with two times the critical dimension is 27-28.

layers.title: What is open
layers.lead: Problems the geometry does not solve, stated honestly:
items: No chiral matter inside Y<sub>7</sub>: disjoint singular loci leave no codimension-7 points (Acharya 1996).
The 43 moduli, Re(T) included, are unfixed at leading order; Re(T) is an open modulus, and values that need it use a labelled calibration (Acharya et al. 2005).
The leading-order flux potential cannot accelerate the universe (slope ≥ 5 √(2/7)).
Flavour structure awaits a chiral sector.
Ghost control of the second time direction has no computed backing, and Nahm's bound on supersymmetric theories with one time (at most 11 dimensions) must be evaded by the 13D(12,1) shadows.

layers.title: Where it stands against data
layers.lead: Above the closed geometry the model’s physics layers carry calibrations, counted in the free-variable ledger, and the model does not fit the data globally. Every comparison — passes and failures alike — is reported row by row in the paper’s results section and on the validation pages.
